garments.name: Aube
garments.description: Bias-cut silk that pours like first light. It moves a breath after you, and lingers long after you leave.
notes: Aube is cut on the bias from a single length of charmeuse, so it follows the body rather than holding it.
Its hem is rolled by hand — nearly four metres of stitches no wider than a grain of rice.

garments.name: Minuit
garments.description: Double cashmere, hand-finished until it feels confided rather than worn. Winter, rendered tender.
notes: Double-faced cashmere is woven as two cloths, then separated by hand at every seam — there is no lining, only softness.
Each Minuit coat passes through the hands of one tailor, from first cut to final press.

garments.name: Vellum
garments.material: Wool and silk grain de poudre
garments.description: A shoulder sculpted by hand, a waist that remembers yours. Authority, whispered rather than spoken.
notes: The shoulder of Vellum is built from seven layers of canvas, padded and shaped by hand over two days.
Its buttonholes are hand-sewn in silk twist — the quiet signature of the atelier.

garments.name: Sérac
garments.description: Baby cashmere knotted into quiet architecture — the warmth of an embrace, the line of a sculpture.
notes: Only the first combing of the kid goat's undercoat is used — finer than fifteen microns.
Sérac's cables are knitted in a single, unbroken thread so the pattern never interrupts itself.

garments.name: Ombre
garments.description: A single sweep of satin, cut to catch candlelight — and to keep your secrets beautifully.
notes: Ombre's satin is woven slowly on vintage looms, giving it a depth that glows rather than shines.
The straps are adjustable by a hidden slider, so the neckline falls exactly where you wish.

garments.name: Lisière
garments.description: Two hundred sun-ray pleats, each pressed by hand, opening like a sigh with every step you take.
notes: Each pleat of Lisière is set between card moulds and steamed by hand — a craft passed down through three generations.
When you are still, it falls as a column. When you walk, it blooms.

garments.name: Calme
garments.description: Sea Island cotton, impossibly crisp and softly dramatic at the cuff. The art of perfect restraint.
notes: Sea Island cotton is the rarest in the world — less than a fraction of one percent of all cotton grown.
The collar of Calme is cut by hand and never fused, so it softens to you over the years.

garments.name: Rivage
garments.description: Fluid wool falling in one unbroken line from waist to floor. Length, effortlessly given.
notes: Rivage is pressed with a single, razor-sharp crease that our pressers set by eye, never by machine.
The waistband is shaped with a curved seam so it sits higher, and kinder, than any straight band.

garments.name: Noctis
garments.description: Midnight silk velvet with grosgrain lapels — made for the moment the room turns to look.
notes: Velvet must be cut with its pile all running one way; Noctis is laid out panel by panel under a single lamp.
The lapels are faced in grosgrain woven in a small mill that has made only ribbon for a century.

garments.name: Albâtre
garments.description: Alabaster jersey draped directly on the form, falling into folds a sculptor would envy.
notes: Albâtre is draped on a living form, not a pattern — every fold is pinned where it wished to fall.
Its silk jersey weighs barely anything, yet holds a drape as if carved.

garments.name: Brume
garments.description: Our trench, reimagined in mist-grey cashmere. Rain was never quite this romantic.
notes: Brume's gabardine is woven so densely it turns away a passing shower, yet drapes like a cardigan.
The horn buttons are cut and polished by hand; no two share quite the same pattern.

garments.name: Ardent
garments.description: Sheer organza with a softly ruffled collar — a breath of romance, held with perfect poise.
notes: Organza is unforgiving: one wrong stitch shows. Ardent's seams are French-finished, invisible from either side.
Its ruffle is cut on a spiral, so it falls in soft waves instead of gathers.
